omitted_axes.reason: Issue #76 exposes application and HTTP contracts only; no user interface is in scope.

test_cases.requirement: Proposal intent binds one deeply immutable policy snapshot and matching digest.
test_cases.risk: Caller-owned nested mutation can change approval or expiry semantics after digest validation.
steps: Construct policy provenance from nested caller-owned mappings and sequences.
Attempt top-level and nested source/retained-value mutation before and after proposal creation.
Reload the proposal and recompute canonical policy digest.
expected_results: No retained policy semantic can be mutated.
The proposal snapshot and digest remain internally consistent.
Policy-selected expiry semantics are part of the attested snapshot.

test_cases.requirement: Invalid input and unverified m4r1 targets fail before persistence.
test_cases.risk: Spoofed authority or target claims can become durable proposal intent.
steps: Exercise the complete parameter and forbidden-field matrix.
Exercise malformed, tampered, expired, revoked, cross-Workspace and store-mismatch references.
Inspect response and counters.
expected_results: Invalid input maps to the closed 400/403/422 envelopes.
Rejected requests create no proposal, decision or audit rows.
No provider write occurs.

test_cases.requirement: Authentication and Workspace authorization precede proposal lookup.
test_cases.risk: Cross-Workspace requests can leak proposal existence or mutate another tenant.
steps: Call create/read/approve/reject without authentication and from the wrong Workspace.
Read and decide an absent proposal as an authorized principal.
expected_results: 401/403 occurs before lookup.
Authorized absence is 404.
Denied calls add no decision/audit row and no provider write.

test_cases.requirement: Only currently authorized humans decide; separation of duties is policy-selected.
test_cases.risk: Model/system approval or blanket proposer inequality can corrupt authority semantics.
steps: Attempt decisions from model, system and unauthorized human contexts.
Approve the same actor under no-SoD and explicit-SoD policies.
Exercise the closed reject-reason set and one unknown value.
expected_results: Only authorized human decisions persist.
SoD denies only when explicitly configured.
Unknown reject reason fails before persistence; approval grants no execution authority.

test_cases.requirement: Concurrent approve/reject has one deterministic atomic winner.
test_cases.risk: Two decisions can commit or retries can overwrite the winner.
steps: Release concurrent approve and reject commands against one expected revision.
Reload and retry both decisions.
expected_results: Exactly one decision and one decision audit event persist.
Revision increments once.
Losers/repeats return the persisted winner without provider writes.

test_cases.requirement: PostgreSQL reconstructs every immutable provenance field and material replacement creates a new identity.
test_cases.risk: Mapping omissions, mutable rows or inherited approval can silently change approved intent.
steps: Persist, decide, restart the store and compare every caller/actor/capability/binding/policy/reference/parameter/logical-ID/timestamp/audit field.
Attempt material and audit update/delete operations.
Create replacements after policy, title and target changes.
expected_results: Read-back exactly matches the original immutable values and ordered decision audit.
Database guards reject mutation.
Each material replacement has new proposal and logical IDs with no inherited decision.

test_cases.requirement: Production composition derives policy-selected expiry and durable projections distinguish denial, stale mismatch and expiry.
test_cases.risk: A hard-coded lifetime or fake-only clock can diverge from the policy digest approved by a human.
test_cases.seam: RegistryCapabilityResolver production composition plus PostgreSQL read-back
steps: Create an approved proposal through real registry/reference composition using a non-default policy lifetime.
Restart the store and observe temporary execution denial, each capability/binding/policy mismatch and post-expiry projection.
Restore exact compatibility between observations.
expected_results: expires_at equals trusted creation time plus the policy-selected lifetime and the lifetime is digest-bound.
Temporary denial leaves approved/non-stale; material mismatches are stale; expiry is non-executable.
Observations survive durable reload and do not invoke execution, reconciliation or provider write.

test_cases.requirement: One canonical-json-v1 authority and a reconciled #75 integration boundary produce zero provider writes.
test_cases.risk: Duplicate canonicalizers diverge or acceptance reports an unobserved zero-write result.
test_cases.seam: module dependency inventory, counting gateway sentinel and governed verification
steps: Prove proposal code imports the single knora.tools.contracts canonical implementation and run its conformance suite.
Run core #76 tests with protocol fakes and integration tests with accepted #75 CapabilityRegistry/ReferenceVerifier composition.
Run focused/full tests, Ruff, Compose and clean Alembic migration while the write sentinel is installed.
expected_results: No proposal_contracts duplicate authority remains.
Core workflow retains narrow protocol dependencies while the integration adapter may consume concrete accepted #75 seams.
The explicit create_ticket provider-write counter remains zero and all governed checks pass.
